- Counterbalancing residual non-CO2 emissions with CO2 removals will lead to net-negative CO2 emissions at the time of net zero GHG emissions [1].
- Globally, net zero might involve some countries already reaching net-negative levels while others are given more time [1].
- Countries with net zero targets have begun integrating CDR into national pathways and research efforts, but this has not yet extended to net-negative targets and policies [1].
- Many CDR processes have medium to low technology readiness levels and are therefore subject to significant uncertainty [1].

- The choice of methods, and the scale and timing of their deployment, will depend on the ambition of gross emissions cuts, how sustainability and feasibility constraints are managed, and how political preferences and social acceptability evolve [1].
